findings.evidence: lean_versions.py:104-108 `max(names, key=release_key)`; resolve_deps.py:172 `{sha: name for name, sha in lean_versions.release_tags(gh, repo).items()}` (last wins) and resolve_deps.py:268-269; test_lean_versions.py:77-79 `test_release_tag_of_prefers_the_final_release_over_its_rc` shows the collision is considered real; mathlib_cache.py:66 `any(run["head_branch"] == tag ...)` makes the choice of tag observable.
findings.fix: Put the mapping in lean_versions: `release_tags_by_commit(gh, repo)` returning {sha: newest trusted tag} (group `release_tags`, `max(..., key=release_key)`, filtered by `is_trusted_release_tag`), define `release_tag_of` as a lookup into it, and have `Source.release_tags` (resolve_deps.py:169-173) / `Resolver.__init__` use it instead of inverting and filtering inline.
findings.issue: `self.tags = {sha: name for sha, name in src.release_tags(...).items() if lean_versions.is_trusted_release_tag(name)}` computes the same thing as the `release_tag_of` this PR adds (lean_versions.py:104-108), but picks a different tag when one commit carries two trusted tags: the resolver keeps whichever comes last in the ref listing (matching-refs is lexicographic, so `v4.35.0-rc1` beats `v4.35.0`), while the guard takes `max(names, key=release_key)` — the final release. The tag is what both then pass to `release_cache_published`, which matches it against `run["head_branch"]`, so the resolver can propose a rev whose cache the guard looks for under a different tag and refuses. That is exactly the resolver/guard disagreement lean_versions.py:3-5 and mathlib_cache.py:3-4 exist to prevent.

findings.fix: Pass `$(dirname "$0")` to the heredoc as the other two heredocs in this file do (lines 210-221, 267-281), `from bump_manifest import shape`, and report `shape(which, m)`'s problems instead of the hand-rolled checks.
findings.issue: The `direct_deps` heredoc's `load()` re-implements manifest shape validation — packages is a list, entries are objects, names unique — that this same PR extracted as `bump_manifest.shape(name, m)` (bump_manifest.py:59-72). The copy is already weaker: it omits `shape`'s "package without a string name" check and so builds `{None: entry}` for a nameless package, and its wording differs ("manifest has no list of package objects" vs "is not an object with a `packages` list").

summary: The prior awk duplication is fixed and most of the diff reuses the shared modules well. Two near-clones remain: the resolver re-derives "the trusted release tag on a commit" inline instead of the new `lean_versions.release_tag_of`, with a different tie-break, and `check-bump.sh`'s `direct_deps` heredoc re-implements `bump_manifest.shape`.
